Two corrections this submission makes to itself

Both are recorded rather than quietly fixed, because a project that cannot be checked is not evidence.

1 · A withdrawn shade claim

An earlier version claimed 99.2% annual shade. A flat 9 m canopy at 5.5 m does not shade a 9 m walkway when the sun is low and to the south — the shadow slides off the path. The section was re-solved: a narrower walk, a wider overhang, a lower plane, and a deep southern louvre. Measured across all 4,402 annual daylight hours:

ModelAnnual shade on the walk
Previously claimed99.2%
Canopy and louvre alone87.28%
Per m², with the tree avenue counted88.5%

2 · Three withdrawn images

Three visuals presented invented data as measurement: a “CFD thermal comfort analysis” when no CFD was run, a “satellite NDVI” raster that is numpy noise, and an “algorithmically solar-optimised” canopy mesh in which nothing was optimised. All three are withdrawn on the same principle as the 99.2%: anything that cannot survive being checked should not be in front of a juror.

The machine learning

Four models. The constraint on all of them: the target must not be recoverable from the inputs by algebra. The heat index is a closed-form function of temperature and humidity, so "predicting" it from temperature and humidity is arithmetic wearing a lab coat.

ModelTaskResultWhy it is a real problem
Random ForestShade surrogateR² 0.998Learns a slow ray-traced simulation from cheap plan geometry
Neural networkShade surrogate (deployed)R² 0.994Differentiable, so it can sit inside a layout optimiser
Gradient BoostingComfort band, 4-class97.5%Temperature and humidity withheld — sun position and calendar only
K-MeansMicroclimate regimesk = 2Unsupervised; k selected by silhouette, not chosen

Figures

One visual system across every chart — one palette, validated for colour-vision deficiency; no dual axes anywhere; a source line on every figure.

Honesty notes

The full version is in DATA_SOURCES.md.

  • The climate record is 39 years (NCM 1977–2015) but published as monthly normals. The 8,760-hour series is reconstructed from it, verified back against those normals to within 0.39 °C, and labelled MODELLED everywhere it appears. Conclusions are about a typical year, never about extremes.
  • The site boundary is assumed — a 150 × 100 m rectangle pending confirmation against the supplied DWG. Every area figure depends on it.
  • Visitor demand is a scenario model, not a machine learning result. It is deliberately excluded from the model suite: a model trained on it would only recover the assumption that produced it.
  • Diffuse radiation is excluded from the shade model, so shaded comfort is stated conservatively.
